audit.whatIsWrong: Chart reads Skill/Shen/Shen/Skill/Skill/Shen/Shen; the packet chart is Shen/Shen/Shen/Shen/Malphite/Skill/Shen and the audited mirror concluded Shen owns levels 2-3 and both item stages with Malphite's only clear window at level 6.
audit.why: Shen's max-health magic damage ignores the armour Malphite stacks, so the pre-6 levels are his; Unstoppable Force at 130s is the one stage Malphite genuinely owns; first item is a wash while Malphite buys resistances. 56.91% supports the shape.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 3 flip to Shen, row 4 to Malphite at 4/10, row 5 to Skill; difficulty dropped from 6/10 to 4/10 to match the mirror's 7/10 from Malphite's side.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] and whys[4] describe the spikes without a single cooldown, and spikes[0] rests on a false stat claim.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100s — the mid-game clock this lane runs on. Granite Shield absorbs up to 10% of his max health and recharges only after he goes unhit, which is the real pre-commit chore.
audit.corrected: spikes[0] rebuilt around Granite Shield's 10% absorb and the level-2 taunt; whys[4] now names the 130s timer.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] and spikes[0] claim Malphite has 'near-zero magic resistance', which is not true and not in the data. wants.foe[1] says Thunderclap 'procs his passive armor gain' — Granite Shield is a damage-absorbing shield, not an armour buff, and Thunderclap's aftershocks apply ON-HIT effects, which the page never mentions.
audit.why: Riot text: Granite Shield absorbs damage up to 10% of max health and recharges when he has not been hit; Thunderclap carries the onHit flag and is an auto-attack reset. Spirit's Refuge still blanks those aftershock attacks, which the page gets right.
audit.corrected: whys[0] and spikes[0] replace the MR claim with the armour-is-irrelevant point plus popping Granite Shield; wants.foe[1] states the on-hit application instead of a nonexistent armour proc.

audit.why: Malphite's Q and E both carry a derived 'grounding' flag and missingInteractions would have me write that they shut off Shadow Dash and Stand United. Riot's own text says Seismic Shard steals move speed and Ground Slam slows attack speed — no grounding. Matching the mirror, I wrote nothing of the kind. The three suspectNames hits ('Unstoppable Force') are false positives: that is the real R name.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Unstoppable Force and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 4/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Unstoppable Force and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 6/10, Malphite carry threat 7/10.
edits.after: Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10, Malphite carry threat 7/10.

edits.before: Malphite has near-zero base magic resistance — your Q empowered autos deal magic damage he cannot trade back from level 1 onward.
edits.after: Twilight Assault hits for max health as magic damage, so his armour stack does nothing — but pop Granite Shield, it eats 10% of his HP.

edits.before: Unstoppable Force comes online and is the only tool that can flip this matchup — disengage or bait it before committing any all-in.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force is live on a 130s cooldown — it is his one window, so bait it or hold your dash until you watch him spend it.

edits.before: Malphite has near-zero magic resistance at level 1 — your Q empowered autos deal magic damage he cannot trade back, and getting E at level 2 lets you taunt him into the blade for a free all-in before he can disengage.
edits.after: Granite Shield absorbs 10% of his max health, so poke it off before you commit — then Twilight Assault's max-health magic damage ignores the armour he stacks, and level 2 Shadow Dash taunts him into the blade.

edits.before: W-empowered auto to proc his passive armor gain and out-trade you short
edits.after: Thunderclap aftershocks apply on-hit and out-trade you inside Granite Shield

notes: All three suspectNames flags are false positives — Unstoppable Force is the correct R name. Not written, deliberately: the missingInteractions 'grounding' headline for Seismic Shard and Ground Slam, which Riot's descriptions contradict (move-speed steal, attack-speed slow). That flag pair needs a central fix; it will tempt every Malphite agent into telling players a taunt dash can be grounded. The long `early` block still contains the same 'almost no magic resistance' fabrication I removed from whys[0] and spikes[0] — it is too long to rebuild inside +/-10% without dropping content, flagged for a later pass.
